初學時可將口風琴鍵盤朝上，用吹嘴由側孔吹氣；短吹嘴便於手持琴身並看見琴鍵，長軟管: A beginner can hold the melodica with the keyboard facing up and blow through the mouthpiece at the side hole; the short mouthpiece makes it easy to hold the body and see the keys, while the long flexible tube lets the instrument lie flat on a table and be played with both hands. Pressing a key opens the valve of the corresponding reed, and the airstream sounds the free reed, with volume changing with the pressure of the breath. A beginner first practises a steady breath, then tries pressing several keys at once.

口風琴常見於音樂教育課程，尤其亞洲；亦用於嚴肅音樂，如史蒂夫·萊希《Melodi: The melodica is common in music education courses, especially in Asia; it is also used in serious music, such as Steve Reich's Melodica (1966). In reggae and dub, Augustus Pablo and Addis Pablo both use it; it also appears in Hermeto Pascoal's singing while playing, in the playing of the funk keyboardist Bernie Worrell on Bootsy Collins recordings, and at the Inti Raymi festival of Otavalo in Ecuador.
口風琴為自由簧氣鳴樂器，音色接近泵風琴、口琴與手風琴。按鍵打開簧片閥門，氣流通過: The melodica is a free-reed aerophone, close in timbre to the harmonium, the harmonica and the accordion. The keys open the reed valves, the airstream sounds the reeds and resonates in the casing. The keyboard usually covers two or three octaves, commonly thirty-two or thirty-seven keys, and the range can run upwards from a low F. The player controls volume by the pressure of the breath; unlike most wind instruments it can sound several notes at once, limited only by the air available.
口風琴的現代形式由 Hohner 於1950年代末發明，但類似樂器自19世紀已在: The modern form of the melodica was invented by Hohner in the late 1950s, but similar instruments had appeared in Italy from the nineteenth century. From the 1960s it entered serious composition, with Steve Reich using it in Melodica (1966); Hermeto Pascoal developed the technique of singing while playing, extending its timbre and harmony. In the 1970s Augustus Pablo made it popular in reggae and dub, and his son Addis Pablo carried on the same line. In 1968 Hohner brought out the Professional model with a built-in pickup; the Hammond Pro-44 and Pro 24-B had built-in dynamic microphones so that they could be plugged into amplification or recording equipment.
口風琴（Melodica）為手持式自由簧氣鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sach: The melodica is a hand-held free-reed aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 412.132. It has a keyboard on top and a mouthpiece at the side hole, and the breath sounds the reeds; two to three octaves are common. It is small and light, and mostly used with children and in music education in Asia; it is also found among composers, reggae and dub players, and at the Inti Raymi festival of Otavalo in Ecuador.
